notes: Initial source-posture packet for the July 28-30 Iran-Jordan-FirstNet escalation candidate. These receipts preserve official and secondary claim provenance. They do not establish orchestration, a FirstNet systemwide failure, Iranian responsibility for network degradation, forced Jordanian alignment, unlawful retaliation, or proportionality.

sources.title: CENTCOM statement characterizing an attempted surprise attack
supported_record: CENTCOM publicly attributed the launch to Iran and characterized it as an attempted surprise attack against U.S. forces.
The statement supplied a stated launch time and claimed interception outcome.
limitations: The statement does not independently prove the asserted surprise condition or disclose the complete intelligence basis.
Native platform metadata, approval history, and any edits or succession remain required.
sources.notes: Preserve the exact original object and distinguish official characterization from reconstructed physical fact.

sources.title: Jordanian air defenses intercept five missiles fired from Iran
supported_record: Jordan publicly claimed its defenses intercepted and destroyed five missiles fired from Iran.
The indexed Petra publication followed the reported launch by several hours.
limitations: The statement does not establish the total number Iran launched.
It does not prove whether an earlier Jordanian briefing or notice existed outside the indexed Petra page.
It does not establish U.S. control of Jordanian disclosure timing.
sources.notes: Use for Jordan's official claim and indexed publication sequence only.

sources.title: IRGC Notice No. 52 concerning U.S. military targets in Jordan
supported_record: The IRGC publicly claimed an operation using several ballistic missiles.
The communiqué described a U.S. air base and a U.S. central-command facility in Jordan as targets.
limitations: The communiqué did not state an exact launch count.
It did not provide a missile-to-target allocation or verified battle-damage assessment.
It did not establish successful impact.
sources.notes: Acquire and hash the exact Notice No. 52 page and preserve the Persian text as the controlling source.

sources.title: IRNA Persian reproduction of IRGC Notice No. 52
supported_record: IRNA Persian reproduced the IRGC communiqué and used an unspecified quantity equivalent to several or a few ballistic missiles.
The Persian publication preceded the later IRNA English adaptation.
limitations: IRNA is a carrier of the military statement rather than independent verification of launch effects.
The wording does not validate the Jordanian count of five as the total launch count.
sources.notes: Preserve full Persian text and compare line-by-line with later English and Arabic adaptations.

sources.title: US air base, CENTCOM headquarters in Jordan targeted: IRGC
supported_record: IRNA English carried the IRGC responsibility claim and described several ballistic missiles and two target categories.
limitations: The English report is a condensed adaptation rather than the controlling original communiqué.
It does not independently verify impacts, count, target occupancy, or strategic rationale.
sources.notes: Use with the Persian source, not as a substitute for it.

sources.title: Trump says U.S. will hit Iran hard after attack
supported_record: Reuters reported punitive presidential language including that Iran would be hit very hard and that it was our turn.
limitations: The wire account does not replace the complete original video, transcript, question context, or platform object.
The rhetoric does not independently establish the complete operational basis for retaliation.
sources.notes: Acquire the White House or pool primary object before statement-level promotion.

sources.title: U.S. carries out fresh Iran strikes, CENTCOM says
supported_record: Reuters reported a U.S. operation lasting about two hours and striking numerous Iranian command, missile, drone, coastal-defense, surveillance, and maritime targets.
The reported breadth supports the inference that substantial target preparation predated the missile launch.
limitations: The report does not disclose target-package preparation dates, authorization chronology, classified threat inputs, or independently verified effects.
Prior preparation does not by itself prove orchestration or illegality.
sources.notes: Acquire the underlying CENTCOM release, target list, imagery, and later damage assessment.

sources.title: Joint advisory concerning Iranian-affiliated activity against critical infrastructure
supported_record: Federal agencies publicly warned of Iranian-affiliated activity against U.S. critical infrastructure shortly before the July 28 events.
limitations: The advisory does not identify AT&T, FirstNet, Astound, or the observed July 28 degradation as victims.
It does not prove that the advisory was bait, that the network event was staged, or that cyber activity influenced the strike authorization.
sources.notes: Use only to establish contemporaneous threat context until incident-specific attribution exists.

sources.title: Firsthand observation of concurrent Astound and FirstNet degradation
supported_record: A genuine FirstNet line and an Astound fixed-broadband connection were reported as substantially degraded during the same period.
Both services later improved without local equipment changes.
A non-beta iPhone on the same household network also experienced mobile-service problems, weakening a beta-iOS-only explanation.
limitations: The observation does not establish a systemwide FirstNet failure, a shared network component, cyber tampering, Iranian attribution, or staging.
Provider logs, device records, location history, screenshots, support transcripts, and regulatory records remain required.
sources.notes: Preserve as a firsthand incident report with strict separation between observed degradation and inferred cause.
